thread:
incident-bot: 🔔 INCIDENT: High error rate detected for cross-region routing (eu-west -> us-west). 5xx spike starting ~1753005100. Affected: Dedicated pools in eu-west-1 using latency-based routing. Pagering oncall.
jamie: acked. i'm oncall, joining now. what's the scope? :eyes:
incident-bot: Alerts: 12m window, 4.8% 5xx on regional routing proxy, increase in routing latency for eu-west origins. Error class: 502/504 from gateway. Hostnames: *.redwood-inference.com, route tag: latency-route-v2.
alex: seeing same in the routing logs, looks like requests are being sent to us-west nodes instead of eu-west pinned hosts. Some DNS answers include us-west IPs for eu-west endpoints.
priya: @alex can you grep for recent config changes? Could be a rollout of the latency routing policy.
alex: pulled last config change: rollout for latency-route-v2 at 2024-11-06T09:25Z by `deploy-bot`. Policy: prefer lowest-reported latency across regions with >50ms threshold. The rollout targeted 10% then 100% for small tenants. I see a diff where eu-west pinning was omitted for Dedicated customers.
jamie: that explains Dedicated impacted. Paging SRE/networking to confirm if policy exclusion omitted pinned_tag handling.
maria: @jamie we already have customers reporting increased latency and some failing requests. CS queue has 6 tickets flagged P1. Escalating to account teams.
tom: pulling traces — KV cache hit rates normal; errors seem to be upstream 502 from us-west proxies dropping long connections. Possibly overloaded because of sudden traffic shift.
kevin: should we rollback the rollout or patch to respect pinning? Which is faster?
priya: rollback latency-route-v2 rollout to 10% immediately. patch to include pinned_tag would take longer. rollback path:
```
# rollback command (routing-control)
routing-control rollback --policy latency-route-v2 --to-release 2024-11-06-09:25 --target 10%
```
jamie: executing rollback now. tagging incident. @ops-bot reduce TTLs for affected DNS zones to 30s to speed recovery.
ops-bot: TTLs for zones `eu-west.redwood-inference.com` and `dedicated.redwood-inference.com` reduced to 30s (propagation started).
jamie: rollback started — monitoring. alex, can you validate that pinned routes are restored for Dedicated tenants?
alex: checking… nginx routing table shows pinned_tag restored for dedicated-tenant-* after rollback completion. Confirmed: requests now route to eu-west targets for those tenants.
priya: still seeing some 502s as old DNS entries may persist. estimated full recovery in ~2m after TTL.
maria: updating customers: sent note to affected accounts explaining routing anomaly, mitigation in progress, ETA 10m. customers asked for postmortem.
jamie: reduced error rate from 4.8% -> 0.6% over last 3 mins. Latency also stabilizing. Keeping pager for 30m watch.
kevin: we should surface this in the console incident banner for Dedicate customers in eu-west. maria please coordinate copy.
maria: will post banner and follow up with account owners.
priya: root cause hypothesis: rollout omitted honor of 'pinned_tag' for Dedicated class due to a config merge conflict. action items: 1) revert rollout (done), 2) add CI test to ensure pinned_tag honored, 3) run a targeted canary on staging, 4) postmortem + customer communication.
jamie: can someone open a runbook ticket for the postmortem and link timeline? I'll mark oncall handover once stable.
tom: opened PM-1234 with timeline + logs. attaching packet captures and routing diffs.
alex: leaving notes: `diff routing-policy` shows the line that caused it:
```
- allow_override: true
+ allow_override: false  # removed pinned_tag handling
```
kevin: ack. want a hotfix PR that re-adds pinned_tag handling with test coverage. assign to @tom.
tom: will do. PR link: https://git.redwood/internal/routing/PR-482
maria: CS update: all impacted customers notified, several asked for credit; collecting list.
jamie: oncall watch ended, handing off to @priya for post-incident monitoring. I'm switching to follow-up tasks.
priya: taking over watch. If any regression, page SRE and Alex.
incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: error rate dropped below threshold and routing restored. Incident duration: ~12 minutes. Runbook: https://wiki.redwood/incidents/1753005123
jamie: post-incident notes: quick rollback was effective. follow-ups: postmortem, CI rule for pinning, add automated canary for Dedicated class, update runbook to include DNS TTL adjustment as mitigation.
maria: scheduling customer follow-up calls tomorrow. adding owners.
ops-bot: reminder added: runbook review in 48h, owner: priya. :white_check_mark:
kevin: thanks team. good fast response. I'll draft the customer-facing postmortem after internal writeup.
